text:
Maya: @ops-oncall seeing a surge of 502/504 from hosted inference after today's rollout. Error rate jumped from 0.2% -> ~6% starting ~08:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/alerts/inf-502 :rotating_light:
Samir: Oof. Which rollout exactly? kernel/runtime change or config flag flip?
Maya: rollout id=deploy-2026-03-17-rtv2. We ramped canary pool weight 15% -> 50% at 08:05.
Samir: Can you paste a trace id or sample request?
Maya: sample trace id: trace-9fd3a1. Log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T08:13:22Z client=api-router svc=proxy-adapter level=error msg="upstream response 502" path="/v1/generate" status=502 duration=45ms error="unexpected EOF while reading headers"
```
Dave: I'm seeing truncated Authorization header for the same traces — originally ~256 bytes, now cut to ~128 for some upstream hops.
Lena: That matches the canary config we flipped this morning: `trim_auth_header=true` became default in router via PR #4321.
Maya: @deploy-bot shows: canary-config applied -> tag=canary-516 -> namespaces=inference-pool-3.
Samir: If the auth header gets truncated, model servers reject the token and proxy returns 502. We should revert the config flip immediately.
Emily: Oncall, can you rollback the flag and move traffic back to 15%? Customers are complaining.
Ops-Oncall: Ack. Rolling back `trim_auth_header` on canary pool and reducing weight to 15% now.
Support-Bot: Incident INC-2026-345 created and P0 channel notified.
Dave: Repro (from prod-edge):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <very-long-token>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# returns HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
Lena: Quick mitigation: set `trim_auth_header=false` on canary nodes and restart proxy-adapter. Patch PR #4322 created to gate this flag per-route instead of global default.
Samir: Also seeing correlated increase in `kvcache-miss` for canary pool 3 around the same time — might amplify latency and error propagation.
Maya: Rollback completed at 08:27 UTC. Traffic back to 15%. Error rate dropped to ~0.5% in the next 10m window.
Emily: Confirming proxy-adapter restarts done on all canary machines, and config now matches stable.
Billing: Noted. Customers ACME and PixelCo reported increased failed requests. Flagging for potential billing correction window.
Support: Outreach to affected customers started (template sent). Collecting trace ids and sample request bodies for refunds/credits.
Maya: Next steps: 1) postmortem owner and timeline, 2) add canary smoke test that validates auth header passthrough and token validation, 3) tighten config gating so defaults aren't flipped without explicit rollout plan.
Samir: Assigning postmortem owner @Lena. ETA for draft 48h.
Maya: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
